user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
I'll search for current regulatory guidance and recent MM trial PRO strategies to supplement the knowledge graph evidence. ## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This trial needs to demonstrate patient-reported superiority in bone pain and physical functioning while capturing treatment tolerability benefits of weekly step-up dosing versus established proteasome inhibitors.

**Key challenge:** The BPI-SF scores poorly (55/100, no change detection) despite being the obvious bone pain instrument, forcing reliance on EORTC QLQ-C30 pain subscale which lacks bone-specific content validity.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 (regulatory precedent from [TI-002], [TI-003], [TI-004], [TI-005]) + EQ-5D-5L (HTA mandatory) + BFI (fatigue change detection in [TI-005]).

**Critical gap:** Physical functioning domain has no candidate instrument despite being a TPP claim — EORTC QLQ-C30 physical functioning subscale is the only available option but lacks proteasome inhibitor-specific content validity.

## Key Observations

•  In 34 out of 43 clinical studies, either exclusively relapsed patients (n=24) or a mix of newly diagnosed and relapsed (n=9) were included, highlighting the need for updating the conceptual model for the QLQ-MY20  [Table 3, EORTC QLQ-MY20 row] — the 25-year-old instrument may miss modern immunotherapy toxicities.

•  The MCID scores for deterioration were uniformly higher than the MCIDs for improvement  across both EORTC QLQ-C30 and BPI instruments [Table 3, MCID Evidence column] — this asymmetry must inform endpoint threshold selection for TTD versus TTI analyses.

• In 57 KG trial-instrument records, 92% positioned PRO endpoints as secondary with no primary PRO endpoints documented — this precedent supports secondary positioning to minimize alpha control risk while maintaining regulatory credibility.

•  The correlation between BPI pain severity index and the EORTC QLQ-C30 item on pain intensity was 0.70 (P < 0.001)  [Table 3, EORTC QLQ-C30 row] — validates using QLQ-C30 pain subscale as bone pain proxy when BPI-SF is unavailable.

• Item library consideration: Multiple comparator trials used QLQ-C30 and QLQ-MY20 subscales rather than full instruments, potentially reducing patient burden from 50 to ~30-35 items per timepoint — decision for the COA expert whether selective subscale administration is appropriate.

•  Using the distribution-based method, there was good agreement between the 0.5 standard deviation (SD) values and anchor-based scores for deterioration  [Table 3, MCID Evidence column] — provides fallback MCID estimation method if anchor-based thresholds unavailable.

## Comparator Analysis

**carfilzomib** (EMA Accepted) — PI mechanism — used EORTC QLQ-C30 (GHS/QoL scale only) — improved upon peripheral neuropathy profile — supports QLQ-C30 as sensitive to PI toxicity differentiation. **ixazomib** (EMA Accepted) — PI mechanism — used EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 — improved patient convenience and quality of life — provides strongest precedent for the QLQ-C30/MY20 combination detecting PI treatment advantages. **bortezomib** — PI mechanism — no PRO instruments documented — established safety/tolerability profile serves as comparator baseline but offers no PRO sensitivity evidence. **lenalidomide** and **pomalidomide** — immunomodulators — no PRO instruments applicable — represent prior therapy context but not mechanism-relevant comparators.

Based on comparator evidence, **EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 combination has the strongest signal of change in this indication** because both carfilzomib and ixazomib studies demonstrated statistically significant PRO improvements using these instruments in proteasome inhibitor populations with similar prior therapy exposure patterns.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In Candidate List? | Action Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D | Yes — EQ-5D-5L | Ensure UK value set applied |
| ICER | EQ-5D | Yes — EQ-5D-5L | Ensure US preference weights used |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to include BFI despite limited MM-specific validation, given fatigue is a TPP claim and BFI showed change detection in [TI-005].

2. Accept EORTC QLQ-C30 pain subscale as bone pain proxy or seek alternative pain instrument with better MM bone disease content validity.

3. Secondary endpoint positioning for alpha-controlled testing versus exploratory designation, balancing regulatory precedent (92% secondary) against hypothesis strength.

4. Assessment schedule optimization for weekly dosing regimen while maintaining comparability to monthly PI comparators from KG trials.

5. Item library approach using QLQ-C30/MY20 subscales to reduce burden from 64 to ~40 items, following multiple comparator trial precedent but requiring validation of subscale-only administration.
